## Third Verse
<!--Put the first two verses of The Walrus and the Carpenter here!-->


The moon was shining sulkily,  
Because she thought the sun  
Had got no business to be there  
After the day was done—  
"It's very rude of him," she said,  
"To come and spoil the fun!"  

The sea was wet as wet could be,  
The sands were dry as dry.  
You could not see a cloud, because  
No cloud was in the sky:  
No birds were flying overhead—  
There were no birds to fly.

## Last Verse
<!--Put a short poem of your choice 8-20 lines,here!-->

the professor talks about probability.  
like life ever gave a damn about the odds.  
i sit there staring at numbers.  
that promise to explain the universe.  
the mean, the median, the standard deviation,  
all different ways of measuring misery.  
i've got a 13 percent chance of understanding this.  
and a 100 percent chance of needing a drink.  
the bell rings, the numbers disappear,  
and somehow, i'm still below average.
